Rehabilitate West Vehicle Service Road, Design-Bid-Build Contract (District 5) 

This council agenda item approves the City of Mesa to issue a construction contract for the reconstruction of the West Vehicle Service Road at Falcon Field Airport.  This project is approved and has been awarded a construction grant by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT). 
 
This project includes rehabilitating the asphalt pavement and shoulders of the West Vehicle Service Road at Falcon Field Airport. Rehabilitation and reconstruction work is necessary to repair the road and extend its service life.  

Staff recommend awarding a contract to Granite Construction, in the amount of $792,291.00, and authorizing a change order allowance in the amount of $79,229.10 (10%), for a total authorized amount of $871,520.10. This project is funded by Airport Capital Funds and will be reimbursed through FAA and ADOT Grants.  On August 20, 2026, the Mesa City Manager approved an Airport Grant Agreement from the FAA that provides 95.0% of the necessary construction funding for this project.

Construct Taxiway I (Future Taxiway H), Design-Bid-Build Contract (District 5) 

This council agenda item approves the City of Mesa to issue a construction contract for the construction of Taxiway I (Future Taxiway H) at Falcon Field Airport.  This project is approved and has been awarded a construction grant by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and is eligible for a grant with the Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT). 
 
This project will create a new taxiway at the north end of Taxiway D at Falcon Field Airport.  Taxiway I (Future Taxiway H) will connect to the Anzio Ramp and create space for a future holding bay.   

Staff recommend awarding a contract to Sunland Asphalt & Construction Company, in the amount of $629,234.95, and authorizing a change order allowance in the amount of $62,923.50 (10%), for a total authorized amount of $692,158.45. This project is funded by Airport Capital Funds and will be reimbursed through FAA and ADOT Grants.  On August 25, 2026, the Mesa City Manager approved an Airport Grant Agreement from the FAA that provides 95.0% of the necessary construction funding for this project.

Three-Year Term Contract with Two-Year Renewal Options for Storm Drain Pump and Maintenance Repair for the Transportation and Facilities Management Departments (Single Response) (Citywide)

This contract will provide storm drain pump maintenance, and general pump repair services for pumps maintained by the Transportation and Facilities Management Departments. The departments oversee a variety of pumps that support critical City infrastructure and facility operations by managing stormwater, circulating water through heating and cooling systems, and conveying wastewater. These systems require routine inspections, preventive maintenance, and repairs to maintain reliable performance and minimize service disruptions. Regular maintenance and timely repairs also help reduce equipment failures, extend the useful life of the pumps, and support the continued operation of City services and facilities. 

A committee representing the Transportation and Facilities Management Departments and Procurement Services evaluated responses and recommend awarding the contract to the single, responsive, and responsible proposal from RediPump, LLC in a total amount not to exceed $700,000 annually, with an annual increase allowance of up to 5% or the adjusted Consumer Price Index.

Three-Year Term Contract with Two-Year Renewal Options for Traffic Signal LED Replacement Services for the Transportation Department (Citywide)

This contract will provide services to replace LED traffic signal indications throughout the City. LED indications (red, yellow, and green lights and arrows) are routinely replaced as they approach the end of their expected service life to help maintain the reliable operation and visibility of traffic signals. Timely replacement of aging indications helps reduce the potential for unexpected failures, supports consistent signal performance, and ensures traffic signals remain clearly visible to motorists, pedestrians, and other roadway users.

The Transportation Department and Procurement Services recommend awarding the contract to the lowest, responsive, and responsible bidder, B & F Contracting, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $239,417 annually, with an annual increase allowance of up to 5% or the adjusted Consumer Price Index.

Three-Year Term Contract with Two-Year Renewal Options for LED Modules for Traffic Control Signals for the Transportation Department (Citywide)
 
This contract will provide LED modules used for replacements and routine maintenance on traffic signals and school zone flashers. The LED modules include red, yellow, and green round ball indication signals, arrow indication signals, and pedestrian indication signals. 
 
The Transportation Department and Procurement Services recommend awarding the contract to the lowest, responsive, and responsible bidder, AM Signal, LLC in an amount not to exceed $206,000 annually, with an annual increase allowance of up to 5% or the adjusted Producer Price Index.

Five-Year Term Contract for Pool Treatment Chemicals - Group 6 for the Parks, Recreation and Community Facilities Department (Citywide)
 
This contract will allow for the purchase and delivery of pool treatment and testing chemicals for the aquatic complexes, splash pads, and fountains maintained by the Parks, Recreation, and Community Facilities Department. The use of these chemicals ensures that all bodies of water remain in compliance with the Maricopa County and Model Aquatic Health Code rules and regulations, supporting safe use by residents.
 
The Parks, Recreation and Community Facilities Department and Procurement Services recommend awarding the contract to the lowest, responsive, and responsible bidders, Brenntag Pacific, LLC.; Landmark Aquatic Services, LLC.; and Leslie’s Poolmart, Inc. dba Leslie’s Swimming Pool and Supplies in a combined total amount not to exceed $107,000, annually, with an annual increase allowance of up to 5% or the adjusted Consumer Price Index.

Five-Year Term Contract for Electrical Equipment, Part & Supplies for Various Citywide Departments (Citywide)
 
This contract will provide industrial and non-industrial electrical equipment, parts, and supplies, as well as data communications products, to support various projects citywide. Most common items include fuses, distribution panels, conduit fittings, breakers, relays, overloads, contactors, sensors, lighting and electrical supplies, intrusion and access control parts, and motor control equipment. 

The City partnered with the AXIA Cooperative to lead the solicitation that created this term contract. The contract will be available to over 30,000 public agencies nationally through AXIA’s cooperative purchasing program. As part of the agreement, the City will receive a rebate based on all sales against the contract. 
 
A committee representing the Water Resources, Department of Innovation and Technology, Energy Resources, Engineering, Facilities Management, Park, Recreation & Community Facilities, and Transportation Departments and Procurement Services evaluated responses and recommend awarding the contract to the qualified proposals from City Electric Supply Company; Consolidated Electrical Distributors, Inc. dba Arizona Electric Supply (a Mesa business); Elliot Electric Supply (a Mesa business); and Lighting Unlimited in a combined total amount not to exceed $3,520,000.00 annually, with an annual increase allowance of up to 5% or the adjusted Consumer Price Index.

Five-Year Use of a Cooperative Term Contract for Information Technology Temporary and Professional Services for the Mesa Police Department (Citywide)

This contract will provide a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) to support body-worn camera redaction and digital evidence sharing. The TAM will be on-site four days a week and will assist with ongoing system set up and configuration, account maintenance, data analysis and reporting, and provide technical assistance. The Mesa Police Department currently fills these roles through Axon, which has discontinued this temporary staffing function and transferred it to Insight Global, LLC. Transitioning the functions preserves program knowledge and prevents a gap in support for body-worn camera and digital evidence redaction operations.  

The Mesa Police Department and Procurement Services recommend authorizing the purchase using the Omnia Partners cooperative contract with Insight Global, LLC in an amount not to exceed $260,000 annually, with an annual increase allowance of up to 5% or the adjusted Consumer Price Index.
